name: Meilah (Misuse of Consecrated Property — General)
notes: Detailed halakhot of meilah: liability thresholds, stages of consecration, permitting factors, joining of measures, and agent liability — the core subject of tractate Meilah

name: Shiur Peruta for Meilah (Minimum Value for Misuse Liability)
notes: The minimum benefit of one peruta required to incur liability for meilah; disputes between Rabbi Akiva and Rabbis regarding benefit vs. damage requirement

name: Meilah After Meilah (Repeated Misuse of Same Item)
notes: Whether repeated misuse of the same consecrated item by multiple persons each incurs liability; applies to animals and service vessels

name: Period of Fitness for Priests (Ra'ui laKohanim) in Meilah
notes: Rabbi Yehoshua's principle: if a sacrificial item had a period during which it was permitted to priests before being disqualified, no meilah liability applies afterward

name: Agency in Meilah (Shliach b'Meilah)
notes: Rules for who bears meilah liability when an agent uses consecrated property: if agent follows instructions, homeowner is liable; if agent deviates, agent is liable

name: Joining Consecrated Items for Meilah Measure (Tziruf b'Meilah)
notes: Rules for combining different consecrated items or multiple acts of benefit to reach the minimum peruta measure for meilah liability

name: Stages of Offering and Meilah Liability
notes: How meilah liability changes at each stage of the sacrificial process: consecration, slaughter, blood sprinkling, placement on altar, and burning

name: Meilah in Kodshei Kodashim vs. Kodashim Kalim
hebrew: מעילה בקדשי קדשים לעומת קדשים קלים
notes: The distinction in meilah rules between most sacred offerings and offerings of lesser sanctity, including the concept of leniency and stringency of the sprinkling act

name: Growth of Consecrated Property (Gidulei Hekdesh)
notes: Whether growths, offspring, eggs, or milk that develop after consecration are themselves subject to meilah; dispute between Rabbis and Rabbi Yosi

name: Meilah in Libations and Blood (Nesachim and Dam)
notes: Rabbi Shimon's ruling on meilah for blood (lenient at outset, stringent at end) vs. libations (stringent at outset, lenient at end)

name: Consecrated Peruta Among Non-Sacred Money
notes: Dispute between Rabbi Akiva and Rabbis about when meilah is incurred when a consecrated peruta is mixed into a purse of non-sacred perutot

name: Desacralization of Consecrated Money (Pidyon to Prevent Meilah)
notes: Procedure by which one can desacralize a consecrated peruta already sent with an agent by transferring its sanctity to another peruta or vessel

name: Five Sin Offerings Left to Die (Chamesh Chatat HaMeitot)
notes: The five categories of sin offerings that must be left to die rather than sacrificed, including offspring of a sin offering, substitute for a sin offering, sin offering of one who died, one that passed a year, and one that was lost and found blemished after atonement

name: Consecrated Items Fit and Unfit for Altar or Temple Maintenance
hebrew: הקדש הראוי ושאינו ראוי למזבח ולבדק הבית
notes: Rules for meilah liability when consecrated items are fit only for altar, only for Temple maintenance, both, or neither — and how items consecrated empty differ from those subsequently filled

name: Meilah Status of Willow Branches and Siloam Water
notes: Meilah status of water drawn from Siloam for libation before and after placement in service vessel, and willow branches for the altar before and after their placement

name: Disposition of Nazirite Funds Upon Death
notes: What happens to funds set aside for a nazirite's three offerings when the nazirite dies, including disposition of designated sin offering money, burnt offering money, and peace offering money

name: Joining of Impure Foods and Impurities to Constitute Requisite Measures
notes: Rules for combining different impure foods or items of different impurity levels to constitute requisite measures for various halakhic consequences; principle attributed to Rabbi Yehoshua

name: Meilah Status of Inner Altar Ash and Candelabrum Wicks
notes: The ashes from the inner altar and wicks of the Candelabrum may not be used but if benefit was derived there is no meilah liability; if re-consecrated, meilah liability applies
